title: [finding] check-half-states: H44 reads a SESSION ID as a dateless tree tip — 6 of 9 rows on the cloud board are this shape, and the prescribed remedy would manufacture provenance
body:
Filed by the `repo:cloud` execution PM seat (seat post objectstack#6026), session `session_01TAUTP6Yky8QWoHUAPDKNJQ`, at 2026-09-16T07:32Z, from a live H44 row set on the cloud board. ⛔ Not graded here — `finding` grading in this lane is the `domain:skills` seat's.

## Measured

`H44_READING_FRAGMENTS`'s `tree` shape is `/\b(?=[0-9a-f]*[a-f])(?=[0-9a-f]*\d)[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b/` — "7–40 hex characters with at least one letter and at least one digit". **A session identifier satisfies that**, and two spellings in live use on this board do.

Probe, run against `h44UntimestampedReading` from `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` at `origin/main` `cd8df644`, at 2026-09-16T07:31Z:

| input (real shapes, taken off live cards) | H44 |
|:--|:--|
| `Claim: PM session c5c0ce54 — dispatching this card` | **FIRES** · `kind=tree` · fragment `c5c0ce54` |
| `Claim: PM 会话 c5c0ce54 派发本卡（席位 F）。` | **FIRES** · `kind=tree` · fragment `c5c0ce54` |
| `Session: ` + a backticked `session_71836b57-5db6-459d-ae4d-c6d9d7dd2cc6` | **FIRES** · `kind=tree` · fragment `c6d9d7dd2cc6` (the UUID's LAST SEGMENT — the hyphen is a word boundary) |
| ⭐ CONTROL A — a real dateless tip, `reviewed head \`480080c7a0\` of the PR` | FIRES (correct — this is the row's actual subject) |
| ⭐ CONTROL B — the same tip plus `at 2026-09-16T06:48Z` | quiet (correct) |
| ⭐ CONTROL C — `Session: ` + a backticked `session_01TAUTP6Yky8QWoHUAPDKNJQ` | **quiet** |

⇒ The predicate is not broken in general — Control A still fires on the thing it exists for, Control B still clears, and **Control C shows the canonical `session_01…` spelling is already safe** (its base32-ish body carries characters outside `[0-9a-f]`). What it cannot do is exclude a session id written in any *other* shape.

## The live cost, on one board

The sweep run against `objectstack-ai/cloud` at 2026-09-16T07:02Z filed **9 H44 rows**. Reading each cited comment by hand:

- **6 are this false positive** — `#2157`, `#2158`, `#2195`, `#2209`, `#2214` all cite `c5c0ce54`, which the comments themselves introduce with the words 「PM session」 / 「PM 会话」; `#1653` cites `c6d9d7dd2cc6`, the tail of the session UUID printed two characters earlier on the same line.
- **2 were genuine** (`#2249`, `#2279` — my own verdict comments, a real PR head stated with no 取数时刻). Both have been discharged by edit, and the edited bodies now lint clean against this same predicate.
- **1 is unverified** (`#1241`, fragment `132211f2`) — its claim carries a canonical `session_01…` line, so the fragment is probably a real tip, but I did not read far enough into that comment to say so and ⛔ am not counting it either way.

## ⚠️ Why this is worse than a noisy row

H44's prescribed remedy is quoted on every row it files:

> Remedy is an EDIT of that comment adding the time the reading was taken (a tree reading also carries its ref or tip) — ⛔ never a re-measurement written as if it were the original.

Applied to a session id, that instruction asks a seat to **stamp a reading that was never taken**. There is no board state behind `c5c0ce54`; it is who wrote the comment, not what they saw. A seat that follows the row faithfully manufactures provenance, and a later reader cannot tell that stamp from a real one. ⇒ The failure direction is 「a patrol row teaches the wrong discipline」, not 「a patrol row is noisy」.

⭐ It also compounds: the same six comments carry H64 rows saying 「NO session id appears anywhere in its text」 while the text says `PM session c5c0ce54`. One non-canonical spelling, two predicates misreading it in opposite directions — H44 sees a sha that is not there, H64 misses an id that is. Recorded as an adjacent reading, ⛔ not asserted as the same defect: H64 refusing to accept an 8-character shorthand as an identifier may well be correct.

## ⛔ What is NOT asserted here

That the shorthand spelling is acceptable. 「PM session c5c0ce54」 is a prior seat's non-canonical claim, and tightening the predicate does not bless it. **Both halves may be owed** — an instrument that cannot mistake an id for a sha, and a claim template that only ever writes the canonical form. This card carries the first; the second is the skills seat's call whether to split.

## Suggested direction (⛔ not asserted — the skills seat grades)

Exclude a candidate that is *lexically part of an identifier* rather than widening the row's silence: a fragment immediately preceded by `-` or `_` inside a longer token (which covers the UUID tail), or one whose paragraph introduces it with `session` / `会话` / `session_`. Keep Control A and Control B green as the regression pins, and add the three inputs above as cases.
